heading: INT. HARBOR ROAD VETERINARY CLINIC - WAITING ROOM - DAY

units.text: INT. HARBOR ROAD VETERINARY CLINIC - WAITING ROOM - DAY
Mrs. K's beagle is in room two. Dr. Sam says give her ten minutes.
units.name: MO
paren: behind the desk, not looking up from the screen

units.text: I don't have ten minutes. I have a cat who hasn't eaten since Sunday and a boss who thinks I'm at a dentist.
units.name: THE WOMAN
paren: standing at the counter, a cat carrier held tight against her chest

units.text: I'm sorry. I really am. But it's triage. Whoever's worst goes first.
units.name: MO

units.text: He is the worst. Look at him. Look. (beat) You're not looking.
units.name: THE WOMAN
paren: setting the carrier down very carefully

units.text: Okay. Okay, he's not great. Give me one second.
units.name: MO

units.text: Mo, who's shouting?
units.name: SAM
paren: coming through the swinging door, drying her hands on her scrubs

units.text: Nobody's shouting. Yet.
units.name: MO

units.text: Are you the doctor? Please. I'll sign anything. I'll wait in the car. Just look at him.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: Hi there, buddy. Hi. (beat) What's his name?
units.name: SAM
paren: kneeling by the carrier, a long breath

units.text: Biscuit. He was my husband's. Ex-husband's. He left him. He left the cat and not me, which, I mean, tells you something.
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: It tells me he was an idiot.
units.name: SAM
paren: a small smile, still watching the cat

units.text: Wow. Okay.
units.name: MO

units.text: Don't start.
units.name: SAM

units.text: I'm not starting. I'm just saying you've been in this clinic eleven years and you've never once said "idiot" about a client's ex.
units.name: MO

units.text: Are you two--
units.name: THE WOMAN

units.text: No.
units.name: MO

units.text: We were.
units.name: SAM

units.text: Sam.
units.name: MO

units.text: Her name's Jen, right? On the intake form. Jen, if you come through, I'll see Biscuit first. Mrs. K can wait.
units.name: SAM

units.text: Thank you. I didn't mean to cause--
units.name: JEN

units.text: You didn't. She did.
units.name: MO

units.text: Mo. Not here.
units.name: SAM

units.text: Then where? In the supply closet, like last March? On the phone, at two a.m., like last June?
units.name: MO

units.text: I can wait outside, really--
units.name: JEN

units.text: Stay, Jen. Please. (beat) Mo, I was trying to be kind to her.
units.name: SAM

units.text: You were trying to be kind to HER. That's perfect. You've got infinite kindness for strangers and animals and nothing left over for the person who actually--
units.name: MO

units.text: Hey. Hey, folks. Sorry, is this a bad time? Roscoe cut himself on a bottle. It's not an emergency, he's just being dramatic.
units.name: BIG DAVE
paren: pushing the front door open with his shoulder, a golden retriever on a short lead, a bandaged paw held up

units.text: Hi, Dave. No. It's fine. It's a great time.
units.name: MO
paren: turning, composing her face with visible effort

units.text: Is it? Because it feels like I walked in on something.
units.name: BIG DAVE
paren: looking from Mo to Sam to Jen

units.text: I just came in with a cat.
units.name: JEN

units.text: Sure. Sure you did.
units.name: BIG DAVE
paren: nodding slowly, sitting on the bench

units.text: I should have said something. Last spring. Before it got to this.
units.name: SAM

units.text: You should have said something in April. In May. At my sister's wedding, when you danced with me and then drove home alone.
units.name: MO

units.text: I was scared.
units.name: SAM

units.text: You're not scared of anything. You put your arm inside a horse.
units.name: MO

units.text: A horse doesn't look at me like you do.
units.name: SAM

units.text: Should we go?
units.name: JEN

units.text: Absolutely not.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: Say it again.
units.name: MO
paren: a long beat, then, very still

units.text: A horse doesn't look at me like you do.
units.name: SAM

units.text: No. The other thing. The first thing.
units.name: MO

units.text: I was scared. I'm still scared. I'm scared right now.
units.name: SAM

units.text: God. You are such an idiot.
units.name: MO
paren: a breath, then a laugh that breaks into something else

units.text: That's what I said about him.
units.name: SAM
paren: wiping her eyes with the back of her wrist

units.text: This is better than the cat.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: It really is.
units.name: JEN
paren: a startled laugh, then a nod

units.text: Go see Biscuit. Both of you. I'll hold the front.
units.name: MO
paren: coming around the desk at last

units.text: And after?
units.name: SAM

units.text: After, you buy me a coffee and you say all of it again. In daylight. Where nobody's watching.
units.name: MO

units.text: I'm watching.
units.name: BIG DAVE

units.text: Dave.
units.name: MO

units.text: Right. Sorry. Roscoe and I will be over here. Being dramatic.
units.name: BIG DAVE
